name: HubSpot

verdict.headline: OAuth works immediately in developer test accounts; sign the AUP to install unlisted in up to 25 production accounts, and get 3 active unaffiliated installs before you can submit a Marketplace listing.
verdict.nextAction: Create a HubSpot developer account, install and authenticate HubSpot CLI v7.6.0+, and sign the Acceptable Use Policy so the app can install outside developer test accounts.

appType: Marketplace-distribution OAuth app built as a project on developer platform 2025.2 or later (new legacy public apps cannot be created since 2026-06-23)

paths.name: Unlisted (up to 25 installs)
paths.whenThisApplies: You install the app into a small number of customer accounts without a Marketplace listing. Developer test accounts don't count toward the 25.

timeline.label: Account, CLI, project and OAuth server
Sign the AUP and run test installs
timeline.note: Under 1 day. HubSpot states no SLA for the AUP.

timeline.label: Customer admin installs the app
timeline.note: Minutes per install. If the customer's org uses an app approval workflow, that has no stated SLA.

paths.name: App Marketplace listing
paths.whenThisApplies: You need more than 25 installs or a public App Marketplace listing. Approval removes the 25-install cap.

timeline.label: Account, CLI, project and OAuth server
AUP, test installs and 3 active unaffiliated production installs
timeline.note: The AUP and test installs take under 1 day (estimated). Getting 3 unaffiliated production accounts with activity in the last 30 days depends on your customers.

timeline.label: First response from HubSpot on the listing
timeline.note: HubSpot states an initial review within 10 business days. This is the first response, not the full review time.

timeline.label: Address review feedback
timeline.note: Up to 60 days from when feedback is shared. Unknown whether the review clock pauses during revisions.

timeline.label: Customer admin installs the app
timeline.note: Minutes per install. If the customer's org uses an app approval workflow, that has no stated SLA.

beforeApproval.item: Unlisted Marketplace-distribution apps on platform 2025.2+ can be installed in 25 accounts. Developer test accounts don't count. The cap lifts when the listing is approved.
Private OAuth distribution allows 10 allowlisted accounts, or 100 for a Solutions Partner portal.
Until the AUP is signed, a Marketplace OAuth app installs only into developer test accounts.
Installers have to tick "authorize an unverified app".

prerequisites.item: A HubSpot developer account, with Super Admin rights to submit a listing.
HubSpot CLI v7.6.0 or later, authenticated with `hs account auth`.

prerequisites.detail: HubSpot doesn't host one. A Node quickstart is provided.
Without it the app installs only into developer test accounts.

prerequisites.item: Acceptance of the Technology Partner Program Agreement.
Live public URLs for setup docs, support, Terms of Service, Privacy Policy and pricing.
3 active installs from unaffiliated production accounts before you can list.
prerequisites.detail: Each must make API calls or signed requests within the last 30 days.

steps.title: Create a developer account and set up the CLI
steps.detail: Create a HubSpot developer account, install HubSpot CLI v7.6.0 or later, and authenticate with `hs account auth`.
steps.agentHelp: Find the current CLI install instructions and write out the exact commands to run.

steps.title: Create the project
steps.detail: Run `hs project create` and choose App, Marketplace distribution and OAuth.

steps.title: Upload the project
steps.detail: Run `hs project upload` to trigger the build.

steps.title: Copy the client credentials
steps.detail: Copy the Client ID and secret from the project's Auth tab into the OAuth server.

steps.title: Implement the OAuth flow
steps.detail: Send the user to `app.hubspot.com/oauth/authorize` with `client_id`, `scope`, `redirect_uri`, optional `optional_scope` and `state`. Exchange the code at `POST api.hubspot.com/oauth/v3/token`, then refresh with `grant_type=refresh_token`.

steps.title: Test install
steps.detail: Create a test account. On the Distribution tab, add a test install and connect.
steps.agentHelp: Write a test checklist covering the authorize redirect, code exchange and token refresh.

steps.title: Sign the AUP
steps.detail: Sign the Acceptable Use Policy so the app can be installed into standard (production) accounts.

steps.title: Customer installs the app
steps.detail: The installer needs Super Admin or the App Marketplace Access permission, plus the permissions the requested scopes imply.

steps.title: Get 3 active unaffiliated installs
steps.detail: Get 3 unaffiliated production accounts making API calls or signed requests within 30 days.
steps.agentHelp: Draft a pilot outreach note and install instructions for customers.

steps.title: Create and submit the listing
steps.detail: Go to Development, then App Listings, then Create listing. Complete the 7 tabs, run validation, then Agree & submit.
steps.agentHelp: Draft the listing copy, setup docs, privacy policy and Terms of Service, and check them against the submission checklist.

steps.title: HubSpot reviews the listing
steps.detail: The Ecosystem Quality team reviews manually and replies by email.

steps.title: Address review feedback
steps.detail: Fix what the reviewers raise. Once approved, the 25-install cap is removed.
steps.agentHelp: Turn the review email into a fix list and draft the changes and replies.

submissionChecklist.item: OAuth is the only auth method, using one app ID and client ID.
submissionChecklist.detail: No redirecting to, or depending on, another app.

submissionChecklist.item: One use case per app, not a duplicate of an existing listing.
3 or more active installs from unaffiliated accounts.

submissionChecklist.detail: Scopes some users won't have are marked conditional or optional. The "Shared data" table matches the scopes.

submissionChecklist.item: If you request read and write on an object, the sync is advertised as bi-directional.

submissionChecklist.detail: Apps with app cards request no sensitive-data scopes.
Name, company, tagline, install option, 800×800 icon, support email and support languages.

submissionChecklist.item: Setup docs, ToS, privacy policy and support URLs are live.
submissionChecklist.detail: Max 250 characters each. The HubSpot Crawler is allowlisted.

submissionChecklist.item: Brand and trademark guidelines are followed.
AI connectors use user-level permissions and HubSpot's MCP Server.

gotchas.title: Access token lasts 30 minutes
gotchas.detail: `expires_in` is 1800. Read `expires_in` instead of hard-coding it, because older docs showed 21600. An expired refresh token returns `invalid_grant`.

gotchas.title: Refresh token lifetime is only in a blog post
gotchas.detail: A HubSpot blog says the refresh token doesn't expire until the app is uninstalled or the token is revoked. The reference docs say nothing.

gotchas.title: A conditionally required scope can fail the install
gotchas.detail: Required scopes must appear in the install URL's `scope` parameter. If a conditionally required scope is in the URL and the user lacks that feature (for example a tier-gated scope), the install fails. The `oauth` scope is added by default. Sensitive scopes are mostly Enterprise-only.

gotchas.title: Legacy apps
gotchas.detail: No new legacy public apps can be created since 2026-06-23. Existing ones keep working without new features. Migrating an unlisted legacy app with more than 25 installs to 2025.2+ auto-enforces the 25-install cap.

gotchas.title: Platform versions
gotchas.detail: 2025.1 apps had to migrate by 2026-08-01. 2025.2 is supported through March 2027. 2026.03 is current. Listing is refused on unsupported versions.

gotchas.title: Changing the uid creates a new app
gotchas.detail: Changing the `uid` after upload creates a new app.

gotchas.title: Certification is separate from listing
gotchas.detail: It needs 60 active installs (raised from 6 on 2024-05-15), at least 6 months listed, and a technical review.

blockers.whatToDo: Accept the AUP and program terms in the developer account.
List the app. Community moderators say HubSpot makes no exceptions to the cap.
Run pilots with unaffiliated customers making real API calls.
A Super Admin grants App Marketplace Access, or approves the app request.
Fix the missing fields flagged on Review info.

channels.note: Reply via the listing review emails.

unknowns: No stated SLA for the AUP, the customer's org approval workflow, or certification review.
The refresh-token lifetime is stated only in a blog post. The reference docs say nothing.
One community thread cited "<10 installs" as a migration limit, which conflicts with the official 25.
Whether the listing review clock pauses during revisions.
The AUP-error fix and "no exceptions to the 25-install cap" come only from community threads.
All setup, prerequisite, submission and per-install durations are estimates, not HubSpot figures.
